title: A geometric view of photonic errors
narration: My research explores a geometric interpretation of how photonic systems depart from an intended configuration, and how a mathematical model can describe their return.
caption: Conceptual model • not an experimental result

title: Identity, geometry, and dynamics
narration: The Single Entity Field Interpretation describes proposed identity constraints. The Geometric Worldline Field Model describes trajectory geometry. Dynamic Entity Field Integration proposes a connection between those constraints and their evolution.
caption: Identity constraints → trajectory geometry → proposed coupled dynamics

title: Represent a deviation
narration: In the illustrated example, a reference trajectory lies on a saddle shaped surface. A deliberately introduced vertical perturbation moves the trajectory away from that surface.
caption: Σ: z = 0.25x² − 0.25y²     |     γ(t) = γΣ(t) + (0, 0, 0.15 cos t)

title: Apply the prescribed projection
narration: A prescribed vertical projection then returns the trajectory to the surface. The residual becomes zero by construction. This verifies the chosen mathematical operation, rather than demonstrating physical quantum error correction.
caption: Πᵥ(x, y, z) = (x, y, 0.25x² − 0.25y²)     |     rafter = 0

title: Connect the model to physics
narration: The next step is to connect these geometric quantities to measurable optical behavior, specify a physically allowed recovery operation, and test predictions against established methods and experimental evidence.
caption: Physical mapping → allowed recovery operation → independent comparison

title: Make the work reviewable
narration: The deliverables include reproducible calculations, diagrams, numerical data, and research manuscripts. Together, they present a proposed direction for investigation, with assumptions and limitations stated openly.
caption: Jason Duran Dutton • Independent research • Candidate graphical abstract
